tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[A dense countable sum of singularities] ↗ ex:power-singularity-sobolev-membership 1. ch5:5.2-ex-4\group Sobolev Spaces

Let $\{ r_k\} _{k=1}^{\infty }$ be a countable, dense subset of $U = B^0(0,1)$. Write \[ u(x) = \sum _{k=1}^{\infty } \frac{1}{2^k} |x - r_k|^{-\alpha } \quad (x \in U). \] Then $u \in W^{1,p}(U)$ if and only if $\alpha < \frac{n-p}{p}$. If $0 < \alpha < \frac{n-p}{p}$, we see that $u$ belongs to $W^{1,p}(U)$ and yet is unbounded on each open subset of $U$. \end{example}
